title: Clean and oil the air filter
entry_state: Bike cool, on a stand.
exit_state: Clean, evenly oiled filter sealed in the airbox, cover locked, service recorded.
completeness: Covers cover panel removal, filter removal, airbox cleaning, washing, drying, oiling, greasing the seal and refitting with correct orientation.

required_tools.name: Foam air filter cleaner and a bucket of warm soapy water

required_parts.name: Spare foam filter
required_parts.purpose: Fit if the old one is torn, and lets you swap filters at the track.

critical_stop_conditions: Torn foam or a lifted seam: do not refit it.
Filter not sealing all round its edge: do not start the engine.
Never clean the filter with gasoline.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: The air filter is cleaned every 15 operating hours, sooner in dust, and after every wet or muddy ride. Write down the date, the hour meter reading and how dirty the filter looked last time.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on a firm, level surface on a stand under the frame so it cannot tip while you work.

steps.title: Take off the air filter cover panel
steps.instruction: Pull out the upper and lower edges of the left air filter cover panel to free its two spigots from their rubber grommets, then move the panel forward to unhook its locating tang from the airbox cover.
verification: Cover panel off, grommets still in place.

steps.title: Take out the filter
steps.instruction: Unhook the retaining strap from its spigot, lift the filter assembly out, then free the grommets from the spigots and separate the foam filter from its cage. Look into the airbox and the intake: dirt on the clean side means the filter was not sealing.
verification: Filter out, clean side of the intake inspected.

branches.label: Dirt past the filter
branches.condition: Dust or grit on the clean side of the intake: clean it out completely and check the filter seal and seating extra carefully on refit.

steps.title: Clean the airbox
steps.instruction: Cover the intake opening with a clean rag, then wipe the inside of the airbox clean. Never let dirt fall into the intake.

steps.title: Wash the foam
steps.instruction: Soak the filter in a foam air filter cleaner and squeeze the dirt out. Then wash it in warm soapy water and rinse in clean water. Never use gasoline. Squeeze it out; never twist it or blow it dry, because that tears the foam.
verification: Foam clean, no tears or separated seams.

branches.label: Foam damaged
branches.condition: Any tear, hole or lifting seam: fit a new filter instead, and note it in the record.

steps.title: Dry and oil the filter
steps.instruction: Let the foam dry completely. Then soak it in good quality foam filter oil and squeeze out the excess until the oil is even all over: wet, not dripping. Leave it in the open overnight so the thinner can evaporate before it goes back in.
verification: Filter evenly oiled, not dripping, rested overnight.

steps.title: Refit the filter to its cage
steps.instruction: Fit the filter onto the cage with the arrow on the filter lined up with the arrow on the cage. Spread grease on the sealing face of the filter. Hook the filter to the retaining lugs and press the grommets back over their spigots.

steps.title: Install the filter in the airbox
steps.instruction: Put the filter in with its arrow pointing up, make sure its spigot drops into the spigot housing, and secure the retaining strap on its spigot. Run a finger round the edge: the seal must sit flat all the way round. Remove the rag from the intake before the filter goes in.
verification: Filter seated, strap fastened, rag removed.

steps.title: Refit the cover panel
steps.instruction: Slide the cover panel rearward with the tang in its slot and the edges tucked behind the airbox cover, line the spigots up with the grommets and press it home. Pull on it to be sure it is held.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, filter condition, whether the clean side was dirty and whether a new filter was fitted.

title: Change the engine oil, filter and strainers
entry_state: Engine warm, bike on level ground.
exit_state: New oil at the correct sight-glass level, new filter, clean strainers, every plug torqued, no leaks.
completeness: Covers draining, both oil strainers, filter change, refilling, first start and the dry-sump level check.
excluded: Oil pump or oil line service
Engine inspection after debris is found

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: 10W/50 fully synthetic motorcycle oil, about 0.95 L.

critical_stop_conditions: Metal or debris in the oil or filter: do not ride.
Never rev the engine before the oil has circulated.
Oil level not visible in the sight glass: do not ride.
No additives in the oil: they make the clutch slip.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Oil, oil filter and the two oil strainers are done after the first operating hour, then every 2.5 hours of race use and at least every 15 operating hours. Write down the date and the hour meter reading.

steps.title: Warm the engine
steps.instruction: Run the engine until it is fully warm so the oil drains well, then stop it. Hot oil burns: wear gloves and eye protection.

steps.title: Set the bike upright
steps.instruction: Hold the bike upright and level on firm ground (a stand under the frame is fine if it keeps the bike vertical). If a skid plate is fitted, remove it. Put a drain pan under the engine.
verification: Bike upright and level, pan in place.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.instruction: Remove the oil drain plug and throw away its sealing washer. Remove the oil strainer plug next to the drain plug, then the second oil strainer plug on the left side of the engine. Let the oil run out completely.
verification: Drain plug and both strainer plugs out, oil draining.

steps.title: Remove the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the two oil filter cover fasteners, the cover and its O-ring, and pull the filter out. Look at the old filter and the drained oil for metal or debris.
verification: Old filter out, oil and filter inspected.

branches.label: Metal or debris found
branches.condition: Metal flakes, chunks or a milky oil: do not refill and ride. Record what was found and have the engine inspected.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.instruction: Smear clean oil on the sealing ring of the new filter and push it into the engine. Fit the O-ring to the cover, refit the cover and tighten its two fasteners to 10 N·m (89 lbf·in).

steps.title: Clean and refit the strainers
steps.instruction: Clean both oil strainer plug assemblies and their sealing faces thoroughly. Fit new O-rings and refit both strainer plugs at 15 N·m (11 lbf·ft).
verification: Both strainers clean, new O-rings, torqued.

steps.title: Refit the drain plug
steps.instruction: When the oil has stopped dripping, fit a new sealing washer and tighten the drain plug to 20 N·m (15 lbf·ft).
verification: Drain plug torqued with a new washer.

steps.title: Fill with new oil
steps.instruction: Remove the filler plug and fill with 10W/50 fully synthetic motorcycle oil. With a new filter the engine takes about 0.95 L (0.85 L if only the oil is changed). Pour slowly and keep dirt out of the filler. Refit the filler plug.

steps.title: Let the oil circulate
steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for at least half a minute before raising the revs, so oil reaches every part. Check for leaks at the drain plug, strainers and filter cover. Stop the engine.
verification: Engine idled before any revs, no leaks.

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Wait at least a minute, then with the bike upright and level read the sight glass on the right side next to the clutch cover. Warm, the oil must sit between the middle of the glass and the upper mark; cold, midway between the two marks. Add a little at a time if needed. This engine is dry-sump, so the bike must be level and upright for a true reading.
verification: Level correct in the sight glass.

branches.label: Level low
branches.condition: Add a small amount, wait, and read again.

steps.title: Refit what was removed
steps.instruction: Refit the skid plate if one was removed.

steps.title: Record the change
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used, quantity and anything found in the old oil or filter. Dispose of the old oil and filter at a proper collection point.
verification: Change recorded, waste disposed of properly.

title: Replace the spark plug
entry_state: Engine cool, bike on a stand.
exit_state: New plug at the correct torque, hour meter wire routed as before, tank, battery, panels and seat refitted with every torque.
completeness: Covers seat, side panel, battery and fuel tank removal, plug change with the kit tool, and full refit.

required_tools.name: Spark plug tool from the tool kit

required_parts.name: Spark plug cap
required_parts.purpose: Replaced with the plug at the same interval.

prerequisites: No open flame or sparks nearby while the fuel line is open.
critical_stop_conditions: Fuel leak at the hose connector after refit: do not start.
Plug cross-threaded or tight going in: stop and have the thread checked.
Hour meter not counting after refit: reroute the wire before riding.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: The spark plug and its cap are replaced every 45 operating hours. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.instruction: Work only with the engine cool. Support the bike upright on a stand under the frame.

steps.title: Remove the seat and side panels
steps.instruction: Remove the two rear seat fasteners, lift the seat at the back and slide it rearward off its locating fasteners. Take out each side panel's fasteners and lift the panel off the front locating fastener. The regulator under the seat gets hot after riding.
verification: Seat and both side panels off.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the battery
steps.instruction: Disconnect the negative lead first, then the positive, release the battery strap and lift the battery out.

steps.title: Remove the fuel tank
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel pump connector, pull the filler breather hose from the top clamp and remove the centre tank fastener and spacer. Press the locking device and slide the fuel hose connector off its spigot without pulling the hose; catch the drip with a rag. Lift the tank off and keep it away from heat.

steps.title: Note the hour meter wire
steps.instruction: The hour meter wire is coiled round the spark plug lead and held with two cable ties. Photograph its position and routing; it must go back exactly the same, with the spare wire kept short as found, or the hour meter will not count.

steps.title: Remove the plug
steps.instruction: Pull the cap off the plug. Fit the plug tool from the tool kit, unscrew the plug and lift it out in the tool. Read the old plug: a dark, wet or white plug points to a fuel or air problem worth recording.

steps.title: Check the new plug
steps.instruction: The correct plug is NGK LMAR9AI-8 with a gap of 0.8 mm +0/−0.1 (0.031 in +0/−0.004). Check the gap with a wire gauge without touching the fine centre electrode; if the gap is wrong, use another plug rather than bending it.

steps.title: Fit the new plug
steps.instruction: Start the plug by hand in the tool so it cannot cross-thread, then tighten it to 15 N·m (11 lbf·ft). Push the cap fully on and refit the hour meter wire exactly as photographed.
verification: Plug torqued, cap on, wire as before.

steps.title: Refit the tank
steps.instruction: Seat the front of the tank on its castellated grommets, fit the spacer and centre fastener at 10 N·m (89 lbf·in), refit the breather hose in the top clamp, plug in the fuel pump and push the fuel hose connector on until the lock holds it. Pull back gently on the connector to check.
verification: Tank fastened, fuel line locked, pump plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the battery
steps.instruction: Fit the battery, secure the strap at 6 N·m (53 lbf·in), connect the positive lead first and then the negative, terminals at 4.5 N·m (40 lbf·in). A light coat of grease on the terminals stops corrosion.

steps.title: Refit the side panels and seat
steps.instruction: Refit each side panel: rear fastener 3 N·m (27 lbf·in), the two front fasteners 10 N·m (89 lbf·in), upper fastener 3 N·m (27 lbf·in). Hook the seat slot over the rear fender hook, slide it fully forward onto its locating fasteners and tighten its two fasteners firmly. Pull up on the seat to check it is held.

steps.title: Start and check
steps.instruction: Start the engine, check it idles cleanly and that there is no fuel smell or leak, and that the hour meter counts.
verification: Runs cleanly, no leaks, hour meter working.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, plug fitted and what the old plug looked like.

title: Check throttle free play and set the idle speed
entry_state: Bike on a stand, outdoors.
exit_state: Throttle returns cleanly, free play and idle in range, idle steady lock to lock.
completeness: Covers throttle return, grip free play, cable adjustment at the grip, warm idle setting and the lock-to-lock check.

required_tools.name: Small spanners for the cable lock nuts

prerequisites: Ventilated area: never run the engine indoors.
critical_stop_conditions: Throttle sticking or slow to close: do not ride.
Idle changes as the bars turn: correct the cables before riding.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the idle speed after the first operating hour and then every 15 operating hours, and check throttle free play at the same time or whenever the throttle feels different. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the throttle action
steps.instruction: With the bars straight ahead, open the throttle fully and let go. It must open smoothly without force and snap shut on its own spring every time.

branches.label: Throttle sticks
branches.condition: Any sticking or slow return: do not ride. Record it and have the throttle and cables inspected.

steps.title: Measure free play
steps.instruction: Turn the grip gently back and forth: free play at the grip must be 2–3 mm (0.08–0.12 in).

branches.label: Free play correct
branches.condition: Within range.

branches.label: Free play wrong
branches.condition: Outside the range.

steps.title: Adjust the cables
steps.instruction: Slide the rubber sleeve off the adjusters at the twist grip, loosen both lock nuts, screw both adjusters fully in, then screw the opening and closing adjusters out together until the free play is 2–3 mm (0.08–0.12 in). Tighten both lock nuts and refit the sleeve. A loose lock nut can make the throttle stick.
verification: Free play correct, both lock nuts tight.

steps.title: Prepare for the idle check
steps.instruction: A dirty air filter or wrong free play gives a false idle, so sort those first. Warm the engine fully outdoors and make sure the cold start lever is pushed in. Fit a digital tachometer.
verification: Engine warm, cold start lever in, tachometer fitted.

steps.title: Set the idle
steps.instruction: Idle must sit at 2200–2400 rpm. Turn the idle screw on the throttle body clockwise to raise it or counterclockwise to lower it, a little at a time, letting it settle after each turn.

steps.title: Check at full lock
steps.instruction: With the engine idling, turn the bars to full left and full right lock. The idle must not change. If it rises, the throttle cables are routed or adjusted wrongly: fix them before riding.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the free play, idle speed and anything adjusted.

title: Check the hydraulic clutch
entry_state: Bike on level ground.
exit_state: Clutch fluid at the upper line, no leaks, clutch neither slipping nor dragging.
completeness: Covers fluid level, top-up, leak check and a functional slip and drag test, with the plate inspection interval.
prerequisites: Rags over painted parts: the fluid strips paint.
critical_stop_conditions: Fluid leak or soft lever: do not ride.
Clutch slipping: plates need attention before racing.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: The clutch is hydraulic and self-adjusting. Check its operation and fluid level regularly; the friction plates, steel plates and drums are checked every 2.5 hours of race use. Write down the date, hours and how the clutch has felt (slipping, dragging, lever feel).

steps.title: Level the reservoir
steps.instruction: Clean round the clutch reservoir cap. Turn the bars until the reservoir sits level; if needed, mark its position, loosen the clamp and rotate it level.

steps.title: Check the fluid
steps.instruction: Remove the cap fasteners, cap and diaphragm. Fluid must reach the upper level line with the reservoir level.

branches.label: Fluid low
branches.condition: Below the upper line.

branches.label: Fluid at the line
branches.condition: At the line.

steps.title: Top up
steps.instruction: Fill to the upper line with new DOT 4 fluid from a sealed container. A noticeable drop since the last check means a leak: find it before riding.

steps.title: Close the reservoir
steps.instruction: Refit the diaphragm correctly seated between the cap plate and the reservoir and tighten the small cap fasteners gently — they are easy to strip. Put the reservoir back in its marked position and tighten the clamp.
verification: Cap sealed, reservoir back in position.

steps.title: Check for leaks
steps.instruction: Pull the lever and hold it. Look along the hose and at both unions and at the slave end on the engine for any wetness.

branches.label: Leak found
branches.condition: Any leak or a soft lever that returns slowly: do not ride; record it and have the hydraulics repaired.

steps.title: Check operation
steps.instruction: Engine warm, in neutral: pull the lever and select first. The bike must not creep or lurch. Ride off gently and open the throttle hard in a high gear at low revs: revs climbing without speed means the clutch is slipping.

branches.label: Slipping or dragging
branches.condition: Slip or drag: the plates and drums need inspection or replacement.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the fluid level, any top-up, the clutch feel and the next plate inspection due at 2.5 race hours. The clutch fluid itself is replaced every 90 operating hours or 24 months, whichever comes first.

title: Set the engine map, traction, quickshifter and launch control
entry_state: Bike ready to ride.
exit_state: Rider aids set for the conditions and recorded.
completeness: Covers map choice, switch brightness, traction control, quickshifter use and reset, launch control arming and cancelling, and the holeshot device.
excluded: Engine calibration changes with a diagnostic tool
critical_stop_conditions: Switch lights not responding: check the electrical system before relying on any rider aid.

steps.title: Record the current setup
steps.instruction: Note which map, traction control, launch control and quickshifter settings you ride with now, and the track conditions, so you can compare.

steps.title: Choose the engine map
steps.instruction: MAP 1 gives the standard engine response and traction control; MAP 2 gives full-power response and traction control. A short press on the MAP switch on the left switch housing swaps between them. The MAP switch is lit with MAP 2 and dark with MAP 1.
verification: Map chosen and confirmed by the switch light.

steps.title: Set the switch light brightness
steps.instruction: A long press on the MAP switch changes the brightness of the switch housing lights. Set it so you can read them in sun.

steps.title: Set traction control
steps.instruction: A short press on the TC switch turns traction control on (its light comes on) or off (light off). Start with it on for slippery or hard-pack tracks.
verification: Traction control state confirmed by the light.

steps.title: Set the quickshifter
steps.instruction: A short press on the quickshifter switch turns it on or off. It only works on upshifts from 2nd gear and above 2,500 rpm, and does nothing if you try to shift up from 5th. You still need the clutch for first to second, all downshifts, stopping and pulling away. If shifts feel wrong after work on the shift linkage, a long press resets the quickshifter's learned adaption.

steps.title: Arm launch control at the gate
steps.instruction: With the bike stopped, engine idling and the gearbox in neutral, press and hold the LC switch until its light comes on. Use the clutch exactly as normal for the start. The light flashes during the start and launch control switches itself off a few seconds after the start; a long press on the LC switch or a fully open throttle also cancels it.
verification: Launch control light on before the start.

steps.title: Set the holeshot device (if fitted)
steps.instruction: Engine off, in neutral. Choose the top piston with the lever for the least fork compression or the bottom piston for the most. Push the fork fully down, let the lever go slowly once the piston is in the locking area and check the fork stays down. It releases by itself when the fork is compressed hard, for example on the first braking or a big bump.
verification: Fork held down by the chosen piston.

steps.title: Record what worked
steps.instruction: After the session, write down the map, traction, quickshifter and launch settings with the track conditions and how the bike felt.
